vocab.example: I'm currently working as a financial analyst at a telecom company.
I'm in charge of a team of six engineers.
Before that, I spent two years in customer service.
I led a project that reduced costs by 15%.
We changed the process, which resulted in faster delivery.
What attracted me to this role is the international team.
I'm looking to move into a leadership role.
That's a great question. Let me give you an example.

tasks.title: Match the phrase to its job
tasks.instructions: What does each phrase do? Match 1–6 with a–f.

tasks.title: Complete Youssef's answer
tasks.instructions: Complete the interview answer with one expression in each gap.

items.text: I'm ___ a marketing specialist at a food company in 6th of October City.
I'm ___ our social media and online campaigns.
___ , I worked at an agency, where I ___ a campaign for a large bank,
___ 40% more app downloads in three months.
Now I'm ___ work on bigger regional brands.
___ this role is that you work across the whole Middle East.

tasks.title: Make it more professional
tasks.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so it sounds more professional in an interview.
models: I'm in charge of a team of three.
We introduced a new system, which resulted in faster processing.
I'm looking to take the next step in my career.
What attracted me to this company is its scale.
Before that, I worked at a bank.
That's a great question. Let me think.

items.prompt: I'm the boss of three people.
We did a new system and then things got faster.
I liked this company because it's big.
I worked before in a bank.
Hmm… I don't know… let me see…

tasks.title: Write your interview answer
tasks.instructions: Write your own answer to “Tell me about yourself” (120–150 words). Then write your networking version (40–60 words) that ends with a question.

parts.label: Present
parts.hint: I'm currently … where I'm in charge of …

parts.label: Past
parts.hint: Before that, I … I led … which resulted in …

parts.label: Future
parts.hint: I'm looking to … What attracted me to … is …

parts.label: Networking version
parts.hint: Shorter, more relaxed, ending with: “How about you?”

tasks.title: Prepare for follow-up questions
tasks.instructions: Write 3–4 bullet points (not full sentences) for each question. Then answer each one out loud.

items.prompt: What exactly was your role in the project you mentioned?
Why are you leaving your current job?
Where do you see yourself in three years?

tasks.title: Record and review
tasks.instructions: Record your interview answer as a video or voice note. Check it, then record it again.
steps: Record your answer from Task 4 without reading it.
Watch or listen, and check the list below.
Record a second version that fixes one thing.
Send your best version to your trainer.
tasks.reflection: What did you change in your second recording?
